sections.h2: How do I reach the Moore County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Walk in at 26 Courthouse Square, Carthage, NC 28327. Doors are open on weekdays from 8 am until 5 pm. Letters can be sent to Post Office Box 1210 in Carthage, and the phone line is 910-947-6370.

The county's office page sets out a mission of protecting the public records, preserving them and keeping them open to everyone. Marriage licenses work by appointment: complete the application, then call and press option 1.

The same page carries a notice sellers and researchers should read. Staff are back-filling the index for records dated January 1, 1888 through June 30, 1988, and adding parties as they go, so a name may be missing from the online search for those years. The notice tells researchers to confirm in the paper index books at the office.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the Carthage office accepts it?
sections.html:
A deed arrives finished, signed and notarized, either on paper at the Carthage counter or electronically through a filer. Staff are barred by statute from drafting deeds or advising on them, so a lawyer prepares it first.

The recording requirements page lists what page one of a North Carolina deed or deed of trust has to carry.

  • The name of the person who drafted the document.
  • A return name and address, with a stamped envelope addressed to the filer.
  • The grantee's mailing address, which the Tax Department needs for the next bill.
  • The excise tax stamp on the front of the deed.
  • The instrument type, printed across the head of page one.

The stamp is paid with the filing fee. Moore County's page puts the math at $2 per $1,000 of price, or $1 for each $500 or part of $500. The seller carries that cost as the transferor (G.S. 105-228.30).

sections.h2: Which formatting slips add a charge in Moore County?
sections.html:
A document that misses the state formatting standards still gets recorded, with a $25 non-standard charge added to the usual fee. The standards trace to G.S. 161-14(b), and the Moore County page repeats them.

Formatting checklist posted by the Moore County office
ItemRequirement
PaperLetter or legal size sheets
Top of page one3 blank inches
Remaining marginsHalf an inch on the other sides of page one and on every side of later pages
TypeBlack on white, no smaller than 9 points
PagesSingle-sided only
LabelInstrument type named at the head of page one

UCC filings on the national form and satisfactions are exempt. The register may also skip the charge for small type when the scanned image is legible, and an acknowledgment dated before July 1, 2002 carries no extra charge.

sections.h2: Can a law firm or lender e-record in Moore County?
sections.html:
Yes, for firms that enroll with an approved vendor. The county names three: Epen (eRecording Partners), CSC and Simplifile.

The firm then emails the county a completed Memorandum of Understanding for approval. A homeowner does not need to do any of this, because the firm handling the closing usually holds the account.

  • Electronic filers need the vendor account and the approved agreement on file before the first submission.
  • Paper filings come to the Carthage counter, or arrive by post with a check covering the stamp and fee.
  • Paper or electronic, the same page-one and margin rules apply.

sections.h2: What do recording fees cost, and what is the free alert service?
sections.html:
The fee schedule here is the statewide one in G.S. 161-10: a base price for the first pages of an ordinary instrument, a larger base for a deed of trust, and a per-page charge after that. Paying off a mortgage and filing the satisfaction costs nothing.

Moore County also runs a free Real Estate Recording Notification Service. Once you subscribe, an email arrives whenever a document is recorded under a name you listed. One address can watch up to 10 names or spellings, and the alert covers only filings made after you subscribe.

For a homeowner it works as an early warning against a surprise lien, or a deed filed in your name that you never signed. Heirs settling a parent's estate can watch the parent's name and their own.

sections.h2: What does Census data show about housing in Moore County?
sections.html:
The federal estimate for mid-2025 is 110,619 people, an increase of 10.9% since its 2020 base. The land area is 697.68 square miles, which gave a 2020 density near 143 residents for each square mile.

The 2020-2024 survey figures show a county where about three in four households own their homes.

  • Half of owner-occupied homes are valued above $351,400.
  • Households that own their home: 76.4%.
  • Typical rent: $1,254 a month.
  • Residents at least 65 years old: 25.4%.
  • New-construction permits during 2025: 1,077.

A quarter of residents are past 65, and permits topped a thousand in one year, so the Carthage office sees estate transfers and new construction side by side. A clean chain of recorded documents keeps a sale moving, especially when a house has passed within a family.

sections.h2: What happens at the Moore County Tax Department after recording?
sections.html:
After recording, the Land Records Section at the county Tax Department updates ownership from what the Register of Deeds or the Clerk of Court received. The Tax page lists 1 Courthouse Square in Carthage, 910-947-2255, with weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm.

The latest revaluation took effect January 1, 2023, and the next is scheduled for 2027, followed by four-year rounds. A recorded sale does not reset the assessed value, though a price far outside the assessment can bring an appraiser to the property, per the county's FAQ.

Ask for the current bill and any past-due balance ahead of closing so the payoff appears on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: How do Moore County appraisers find out about changes to a house?
sections.html:
The Tax Department learns about new work mostly through permits. The Appraisal page says the Commercial and Residential Section receives permit data from the county and from Aberdeen, Pinebluff, Pinehurst and Southern Pines, then schedules a site visit to record what was added.

Anything that adds heated floor area counts, and so do decks, porches, patios, sheds, pools and barns. The county still expects owners to report improvements themselves. A seller who finished a garage conversion without telling anyone may find the buyer's inspection and the tax record disagree.

  • Every parcel has an ID, sometimes called the PARID or land record key, that appears on the GIS site and on the bill.
  • The GIS site also shows the field review document and a condensed property record card for each parcel.
  • Customer service at 910-947-2255 can walk an owner through the record.

Checking that card before listing the house catches errors in square footage or features that a buyer's agent will notice.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Moore County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm at 26 Courthouse Square in Carthage. The phone is 910-947-6370, and marriage licenses are by appointment once the application is complete.

faqs.q: What goes on page one of a Moore County deed?
faqs.a: Page one needs the drafter's name, a return name and address with an envelope, the grantee's mailing address, the excise stamp and the instrument type. It also needs 3 blank inches at the top.

faqs.q: How much is the non-standard document fee in Moore County?
faqs.a: It is $25, added to the recording fee when a document misses the state formatting standards. The register may skip it for small type when the scanned image reads clearly.

faqs.q: Can I be alerted when something is recorded under my name?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's free Real Estate Recording Notification Service sends an email when a document is filed under a name you list, up to 10 names per address, for filings made after you subscribe.

faqs.q: Who handles my tax bill after the sale?
faqs.a: The Moore County Tax Department in Carthage lists, values and collects, and its Land Records Section updates the owner record from recorded deeds. Call 910-947-2255.
